description: Add the six WRITE tools as thin @tool functions in three new sibling modules (agent/tools/jira_write_tools.py, github_write_tools.py, servicenow_write_tools.py), mirroring the Task 1 read-module pattern (module-level @tool functions reading settings + calling the shared make_request seam, returning a formatted string, never raising). Contracts are transcribed verbatim in task2-design.md 'Exact tool contracts'. This feature is a prerequisite for FEAT-002 (the hook's WRITE_TOOL_NAMES and the agent's WRITE_TOOLS reference these functions). It does NOT wire anything into strands_agent.py/chat.py yet — the modules are importable and unit-tested in isolation, leaving the package green.
steps: READ FIRST: docs/.agents/tasks/task2-hitl-writes/context.json and this file, then the 'Exact tool contracts' + 'Error handling' + 'Input validation' + 'Test plan' sections of docs/.agents/tasks/task2-design.md. context.json replaces re-exploration — do not re-derive what it states.

Create agent/tools/jira_write_tools.py mirroring agent/tools/jira_tools.py structure. Import: from strands import tool; from agent.config import settings; from agent.tools.http import make_request; and from agent.tools.jira_tools import _resolve_assignee, _fetch_developers (the chosen one-way dependency — do NOT hoist or edit jira_tools.py). Implement jira_create_story(project_id, title, description, priority="medium", story_points=0, assignee=None) -> POST settings.jira_url /stories with body = all params, success '✅ Story created successfully: **{id}** - {title}' (reads data['id']/data['title']). Implement jira_update_story(story_id, status=None, assignee=None, priority=None, story_points=None, sprint_id=None): pre-GET make_request(settings.jira_url, settings.jira_token, endpoint=f'/stories/{story_id}') (default GET), if 'error' in result -> "Story '{story_id}' was not found, so it cannot be updated."; if assignee given, resolve via _resolve_assignee (unresolved -> list developers message); build `changes` from ONLY provided non-None fields; if empty -> "No changes specified for {story_id}..."; else PUT /stories/{story_id} with the changes body, success '✅ Story updated successfully: **{id}** - {title}' from the 200 body. Keep the [WRITE ACTION - REQUIRES APPROVAL] docstring tag. Export JIRA_WRITE_TOOLS = [jira_create_story, jira_update_story].

Create agent/tools/github_write_tools.py. Implement _normalize_files_arg(files) (tolerates a JSON string, a single dict, or a list of dicts; keep {'path','content'}, content coerced to str, drop entries without a path). Implement github_create_branch(repo_id, branch_name, from_branch="main") -> POST /repos/{repo_id}/branches body {'name': branch_name, 'from_branch': from_branch}; on error text containing 'status 409' or 'status 422' or 'already exists' return the SUCCESS string '✅ Branch **{branch_name}** already exists — reusing it. Reply "commit the code" to proceed.'; other error -> '❌ Failed to create branch: {error}'; success -> '✅ Branch created successfully: **{name}**'. Implement github_commit_files(repo_id, branch, message, files) -> POST /repos/{repo_id}/commits body {'branch','message','files': _normalize_files_arg(files)}, success '✅ Committed {n} files to **{branch}**' (+ optional '🔗 {url}'). Implement github_open_pull_request(repo_id, head, base="main", title="", body="") -> POST /repos/{repo_id}/pulls body {'head','base','title': title or head,'body'}, success '✅ Pull request opened: **#{number}** {title}' (+ optional '🔗 {url}'). Retain the real-repo-NAME-discipline and 'COMPLETE file text, never a diff' docstrings. Export GITHUB_WRITE_TOOLS.

Create agent/tools/servicenow_write_tools.py. Implement servicenow_create_incident(title, affected_service, severity="P3", description="", assignee=None, linked_deployment=None) -> POST settings.servicenow_url /incidents body = all params, success '✅ Incident opened successfully: **{id}** - {title} ({severity})'. Keep the affected-service enumeration + severity-meaning + [WRITE ACTION - REQUIRES APPROVAL] docstring. Export SERVICENOW_WRITE_TOOLS = [servicenow_create_incident].

In EVERY write body, wrap the write make_request call so a transport exception (httpx.HTTPError / OSError) is caught and returned as '❌ Failed to {verb}: {exc}' text rather than raised (import httpx). The jira_update_story pre-GET and the existing {'error': ...} dict handling stay as-is; only the POST/PUT call needs the try/except wrap.

Add the propose/approve-aligned unit tests for the tool BODIES to agent/tests/test_write_tools_unit.py (create the file; FEAT-002 will extend it with hook/driver tests). Mirror test_tools_unit.py: monkeypatch make_request per write module with a recording fake and assert endpoint, verb (method='POST'/'PUT'), body, and byte-for-byte success strings. Cover: jira_create_story POST /stories; jira_update_story pre-GET then PUT with only provided changes + not-found + unresolved-assignee + empty-change branches (mock PUT return shaped {'id','title'}); github_create_branch POST /repos/{repo}/branches AND the 409 'already exists' -> SUCCESS; github_commit_files POST /repos/{repo}/commits + _normalize_files_arg cases (JSON string, single dict, list, missing-path dropped, content coerced to str); github_open_pull_request POST /repos/{repo}/pulls with title defaulting to head; servicenow_create_incident POST /incidents with the {id,title,severity} success string; and the transport-error wrap (make_request raising httpx.HTTPError -> '❌ Failed to ...' string, no raise).
acceptance_criteria: The three modules import cleanly: `& "<venv-py>" -c "import agent.tools.jira_write_tools, agent.tools.github_write_tools, agent.tools.servicenow_write_tools; print('import OK')"` prints import OK.
jira_write_tools.py imports _resolve_assignee and _fetch_developers from agent.tools.jira_tools and does NOT modify jira_tools.py (jira_tools.py git-unchanged).
github_create_branch returns a SUCCESS (not error) string when make_request yields a 409/422/'already exists' error.
Every write tool returns a string and never raises on a transport error (httpx.HTTPError/OSError caught -> '❌ Failed to {verb}: {exc}').
Running the write-tool body tests passes and the Task 1 suite stays green (existing unit tests pass; the live integration test SKIPS because the tunnel is down).
No LangChain import is introduced; agent/prompts.py and the Task 1 read modules are unchanged (except the permitted import FROM jira_tools.py).

findings:
FEAT-002 reference data for wiring the hook + agent.

MODULE PATHS / EXPORTED SYMBOLS (import these for WRITE_TOOLS and WRITE_TOOL_NAMES):
- agent.tools.jira_write_tools: jira_create_story, jira_update_story; exports JIRA_WRITE_TOOLS = [jira_create_story, jira_update_story].
- agent.tools.github_write_tools: github_create_branch, github_commit_files, github_open_pull_request; exports GITHUB_WRITE_TOOLS (that order). Also exports helper _normalize_files_arg (not a tool).
- agent.tools.servicenow_write_tools: servicenow_create_incident; exports SERVICENOW_WRITE_TOOLS = [servicenow_create_incident].
- Suggested in strands_agent.py: WRITE_TOOLS = [*JIRA_WRITE_TOOLS, *GITHUB_WRITE_TOOLS, *SERVICENOW_WRITE_TOOLS] (6 tools total).

WRITE_TOOL_NAMES (the six @tool function names the hook must gate on BeforeToolCallEvent):
{"jira_create_story", "jira_update_story", "github_create_branch", "github_commit_files", "github_open_pull_request", "servicenow_create_incident"}.

TOOL CONTRACTS as implemented (verb / endpoint / body) — all use the shared make_request seam:
- jira_create_story -> POST settings.jira_url /stories, body {project_id,title,description,priority,story_points,assignee}.
- jira_update_story -> pre-GET settings.jira_url /stories/{story_id} (existence), then PUT /stories/{story_id} with body = only provided non-None fields (assignee resolved via jira_tools._resolve_assignee). NOTE for the approval summary: the propose-pass summary must be built from tool_use['input'] raw args only (body does not run pre-approval), per the design's 'less rich summary' decision.
- github_create_branch -> POST settings.github_url /repos/{repo_id}/branches, body {name, from_branch}.
- github_commit_files -> POST settings.github_url /repos/{repo_id}/commits, body {branch, message, files:_normalize_files_arg(files)}.
- github_open_pull_request -> POST settings.github_url /repos/{repo_id}/pulls, body {head, base, title: title or head, body}.
- servicenow_create_incident -> POST settings.servicenow_url /incidents, body {title,affected_service,severity,description,assignee,linked_deployment}.

SUCCESS-STRING FORMATS (byte-for-byte, for the model to relay; not needed by the hook but recorded for completeness):
- jira_create_story: '\u2705 Story created successfully: **{id}** - {title}'
- jira_update_story: '\u2705 Story updated successfully: **{id}** - {title}'  (reads id/title from PUT 200 body)
- jira_update_story guards: "Story '{story_id}' was not found, so it cannot be updated." | "Could not resolve assignee '{assignee}'. Available developers: {names}" | "No changes specified for {story_id}. Provide at least one field to update."
- github_create_branch: '\u2705 Branch created successfully: **{name}**' | already-exists SUCCESS: '\u2705 Branch **{branch_name}** already exists \u2014 reusing it. Reply "commit the code" to proceed.' (triggered on error text containing 'status 409'/'status 422'/'already exists')
- github_commit_files: '\u2705 Committed {n} files to **{branch}**' (+ optional '\n\ud83d\udd17 {url}' when 200 body has 'url')
- github_open_pull_request: '\u2705 Pull request opened: **#{number}** {title}' (+ optional '\n\ud83d\udd17 {url}')
- servicenow_create_incident: '\u2705 Incident opened successfully: **{id}** - {title} ({severity})'
- transport-error wrap (httpx.HTTPError/OSError caught around the POST/PUT): '\u274c Failed to {verb}: {exc}' where verb is create story | update story | create branch | commit files | open pull request | open incident.

DEVIATIONS FROM DESIGN: none material. The PROPOSAL dict's 'action' values the design keys [SYSTEM] templates on (create_branch/commit_files/open_pull_request) are the mahalo-dock action names, NOT the strands tool names (github_create_branch etc.) — FEAT-002's build_proposal must map tool-name -> action/system. proposal['params'] keys equal the tool signature param names (repo_id, branch_name, branch, head, base), matching the design's [SYSTEM] templates.
